FOR TENANTS · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Is your landlord late returning your security deposit?

Pick your state, enter the date you moved out and the deposit you paid. The page shows the day your landlord's deadline ran out, the statute it comes from, what that statute says about a landlord who misses it, and a demand letter that fills itself in.

General information, not legal advice. State rules change and cities can add their own; read the statute named in the result and check it before you rely on it.

Your situation

For the letter (optional)

Fill in the state, deposit and dates, then click Check my deadline.

Result

What the statute says about a landlord who misses it

Your letter


    
 

    
Send it in a way that leaves proof (certified mail or email with a read receipt) and keep a copy, photos of the unit at move-out, and your lease.

  


  

    
What it applies, and what it leaves out

    
    
      
  • Deadlines: the number of days (or months) each statute gives the landlord after you move out, counted from your move-out date, or from the day you gave a forwarding address where the state expects one.
    • 
      
  • Covered: Arizona, California, Colorado, District of Columbia, Florida, Georgia, Massachusetts, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, North Carolina, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Texas, Virginia and Washington. Other states are not modelled.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: whether a particular deduction is lawful, whether a penalty applies or how much, local ordinances (some cities have their own rules, for example for interest or earlier deadlines), rules for different property types, lease clauses, and whether your landlord's address for notices is the one you used. Public holidays are not skipped in business-day counts. Statute summaries were last reviewed in October 2026; check the current text.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
How long does a landlord have to return a security deposit?

    
It depends on the state: 14 days in New York, 21 in California and Washington, 30 in Texas, Georgia, Massachusetts, New Jersey, Ohio and Pennsylvania, and 45 in Maryland, Virginia and Washington, D.C. This page lists the period for each state it covers with the statute, and counts from your move-out date.

    
What if my landlord missed the deadline?

    
Many states let a tenant recover the deposit plus a penalty, often two or three times the amount wrongfully withheld, and some say a landlord who misses the deadline loses the right to keep any of it. A written demand is the usual first step before a small-claims filing. This page drafts one; a court decides whether any penalty applies.

    
Do I have to give a forwarding address?

    
In some states, including Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Michigan and Minnesota, the landlord's clock depends on you giving a forwarding address in writing. If you have not, this page says so and drafts a letter that gives it.

    
Can a landlord keep money for normal wear and tear?

    
Generally no: ordinary wear from living in a place is not a lawful deduction in most states, but unpaid rent and damage beyond normal wear usually are. The dispute letter this page writes asks the landlord to justify each deduction with receipts.

    
Is what I type uploaded anywhere?

    
No. It is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent.

We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere by this tool.

    
Everything runs in your browser. Nothing you type is uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (deadline_checked, example_loaded, letter_copied, letter_downloaded) are counted only in local storage on your device. The counts can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.
